citations.assessment: The beginning of Sifrei preserves several direct exchanges with Yehudah Berabbi. The Damascus–Chadrach statement occurs within the cited dispute.
The Midrash has the ivory tower verse, the Damascus testimony and the expansion of Jerusalem as far as Damascus’s gates. The received attribution and gate wording are retained.
The Yalkut preserves Damascus, Chadrach and the Jerusalem gates reaching Damascus. It is under biblical chapter 9, at remez 575 in the linked edition.
Chagigah explicitly gives the ben Dormaskit form and the visit at Lod.
The transmission runs from Rabbi Elazar be-Rabbi Yose through Yose ben Dormaskit and Yose HaGelili, then continues to Yochanan ben Nuri and Eliezer the Great.
The story, the legal ruling and the eyes episode occur together under Psalms 25:14 in this Midrash.
Two named occurrences are attested in the checked Sifra, one on fish and one on bread under scarcity.
The checked Megillah baraita names Eliezer, Akiva, Meir and Yose ben Dormaskit in the received order. The exact reading permits removing the expansion qualifier.
The Midrash explicitly names Yose ben Dormaskit in the Flood exposition.
The received name and the Leviathan ruling are directly attested.
Berakhot identifies the formula “on that day” with the change of leadership. Yadayim opens with that formula. The chronology of the visit is Heilprin’s inference from the parallel.
The Eliezer entry explicitly lists Yose of Dormaskit as a student. This verifies the intended internal pointer.
The Mishnah has the dispute over Ammon and Moab and the visit, the secret verse and the Sinai tradition. The Bavli has the additional narrative of the eyes.

The Bavli gives the command, the receiving of the eyes, the transmission and the prayer of restoration. It includes Elazar/Eliezer readings. The received Eliezer reading accords with Yadayim and Shocher Tov.

holds.reason: The checked Onkelos and Jonathan texts give Damascus without Dormaskit. The narrator may have a different Targum witness in mind. Preserve his etymological report without a verified hyperlink.

holds.raw: ונראה דשם אביו דורמסקית לא שם מקום
holds.reason: The narrator presents the father-name interpretation as inference. The ben form and explicit Damascus origin are both attested. The texts do not independently identify a father named Dormaskit.
